title: Grade 11 Chemistry — Gas Laws: Numericals & Real Gases
description: Boyle's, Charles', Avogadro's laws, ideal gas equation, van der Waals
subject: chemistry

questions.question: Boyle's Law states: at constant temperature, pressure is _____ to volume.
questions.explanation: Boyle's Law: PV = constant (at constant T and n). If pressure doubles, volume halves. P₁V₁ = P₂V₂. Named after Robert Boyle (1662).

questions.question: A gas at 2 atm occupies 3 L. At constant T, when pressure becomes 1.5 atm, the volume is:
questions.explanation: Boyle's Law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂. 2 × 3 = 1.5 × V₂. V₂ = 6/1.5 = 4 L.

questions.question: Charles' Law states: at constant pressure, volume is _____ proportional to absolute temperature (K).
questions.explanation: Charles' Law: V/T = constant (at constant P and n). V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂. MUST use Kelvin temperature. Named after Jacques Charles (1787).

questions.question: A gas at 27°C occupies 2 L. At constant pressure, its volume at 127°C is:
The Ideal Gas Equation is:
options: Both A and C (same equation rearranged)
questions.explanation: PV = nRT where P = pressure, V = volume, n = moles, R = 8.314 J/(mol·K), T = temperature in Kelvin. Rearranged: P = nRT/V. Both forms are the same ideal gas equation.

questions.question: At STP (0°C, 1 atm), 1 mole of an ideal gas occupies:
questions.explanation: Molar volume at STP = 22.4 L/mol. This is a fundamental result from PV = nRT: V = nRT/P = 1×0.0821×273/1 ≈ 22.4 L. (New IUPAC STP = 0°C, 100 kPa → 22.7 L; old STP = 22.4 L).

questions.question: Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures states:
options: Total pressure equals pressure of the largest component
P_total = P₁ + P₂ + P₃ + ... (sum of partial pressures of all gases in a mixture)
Pressure of a gas equals its mole fraction
questions.explanation: Dalton's Law: the total pressure of a gas mixture equals the sum of partial pressures. Partial pressure of a component = mole fraction × total pressure: Pᵢ = xᵢ × P_total.

questions.question: Graham's Law of Effusion states that the rate of effusion is:
options: Inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass
Equal for all gases at same temperature
questions.explanation: Graham's Law: r ∝ 1/√M. Lighter gases effuse faster. Ratio: r₁/r₂ = √(M₂/M₁). Example: H₂ effuses 4× faster than O₂ (√(32/2) = √16 = 4).

questions.question: Real gases deviate from ideal behaviour at:
options: Low temperature and high pressure (molecules closer, interactions matter)
questions.explanation: At high P and low T, gases deviate most from ideal: (1) At high P, molecules are compressed close together — volume of molecules is significant. (2) At low T, intermolecular forces become important.

questions.question: The van der Waals equation for real gases is: (P + an²/V²)(V − nb) = nRT. The 'an²/V²' term corrects for:
options: Intermolecular attractions (real pressure is less than ideal due to attractions)
questions.explanation: 'an²/V²' is the pressure correction — molecules attract each other so actual pressure on container walls is LESS than ideal. 'a' measures strength of intermolecular attractions. 'nb' corrects for molecular volume.

questions.question: Avogadro's Law states that equal volumes of all gases at the same T and P contain:
options: Molecules with the same kinetic energy only
questions.explanation: Avogadro's Law: equal volumes of gases at same T and P contain equal numbers of molecules (regardless of their chemical nature). This led to the concept of the mole and molar volume.

questions.question: Root mean square (rms) speed of gas molecules is: urms = ?
questions.explanation: urms = √(3RT/M) where R = gas constant, T = temperature (K), M = molar mass (kg/mol). Other speed expressions: u_avg = √(8RT/πM), u_mp = √(2RT/M). urms > u_avg > u_mp.

questions.question: The kinetic energy of 1 mole of an ideal gas at temperature T is:
questions.explanation: Average KE per mole = (3/2)RT. Average KE per molecule = (3/2)kT (k = Boltzmann constant = R/Nₐ). This is why temperature is a measure of average kinetic energy.

questions.question: A 2 L container holds gas at 3 atm, 300 K. The same gas at 2 atm in a 3 L container has temperature:
questions.explanation: Combined gas law: P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂. 3×2/300 = 2×3/T₂ → 6/300 = 6/T₂ → T₂ = 300 K.

questions.question: The compressibility factor Z = PV/nRT. For an ideal gas, Z = ?
questions.explanation: For ideal gas: PV = nRT → Z = PV/nRT = 1. For real gases: Z > 1 at high pressure (molecular volume effect dominates) or Z < 1 at moderate pressure (attractive forces dominate).
